description:
Filed retroactively to keep the tracker honest — built in the same session as T-058, immediately after it.

PROBLEM, measured before building: only 38 of 132 observations carried a `context` tag, while 142 of 260 session files did. `zug_save_observation`'s `context` parameter is optional and rarely passed, and `runEndSession` never propagated the session's own context down to the observations written during it. The information existed one level up and was being discarded every session.

Joining observations to their session recovers only ~10 more, so 84 of 132 (64%) are genuinely unattributable. A work/personal split of the existing corpus is therefore not possible honestly.

USER DIRECTION: the historical gap is accepted. "its ok if my previous sessions have a gap, i want to use that data to make future sessions and other users session better." The point is the forcing function, not a backfill.

DELIVERED — two parts:

1. INHERITANCE (src/storage.ts, src/server.ts). New `stampSessionContext(session_id, context)` fills `context` on that session's observations where absent, called from runEndSession BEFORE the observations are read so the written session log and everything downstream sees it. Never overwrites an explicit tag — that is a deliberate act. Rewrites the append-only observations log, so a line that cannot be parsed is passed through verbatim rather than dropped by a parse/map/serialize round trip. No historical migration: it would recover 10 of 84, not worth mutating the log for.

2. SEGMENTATION (web/). `readSessionContexts()` builds a session_id -> context map from the headers of live AND ARCHIVED session files — the archive holds 69 files the dashboard previously ignored entirely, and those cover exactly the oldest observations, the ones least likely to carry their own tag. `resolveContext()` applies explicit-tag > session-inherited > unknown. Filtering is driven by a `?context=` search param rather than client state, keeping the page server-rendered and the filtered view linkable.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT worth preserving: the view segments further than the system does. Pipeline health, the persona browser and the active patterns stay UNFILTERED and say so on screen, because there is one PERSONA and one reinforcement store, not one per context. Filtering them would imply a split the system does not make. If per-context fingerprints are ever built, that is a separate architectural ticket.

HONESTY REQUIREMENT: `unknown` is a selectable bucket, always sorted last (it is a gap, not a category), and a persistent banner states the uncovered share. Filtering to `work` shows 39 observations; without the banner that reads as "39 work observations" rather than "39 of 133, with 84 unattributed".

VERIFIED in the browser against real data: chips render all 133 / work 39 / personal 6 / zug 4 / unknown 84; filtering to work correctly narrows Cadence (peak 35 -> 8, axis starts Jun not Apr, since work tagging is recent) and the type breakdown (55/33/35 -> 15/11/8), while type hues stay bound to their type despite the rank order changing.

Tests: 7 for stampSessionContext (fill-only-missing, never overwrite, other sessions untouched, malformed lines preserved, blank/absent context no-op) and 17 for the web side (header parsing, resolution precedence, bucket ordering with unknown last, coverage math incl. divide-by-zero, filtering incl. the unknown bucket). Root 256/256, web 103/103, both typechecks clean.
title: Work/personal context differentiation — dashboard segmentation + session-level inheritance
